variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Variables are declared with DECLARE and prefixed with @.

data_types.title: Data Types

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Operators include + for both addition and string concatenation.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
IF @score >= 90
BEGIN
  SET @grade = 'A';
END
ELSE IF @score >= 80
BEGIN
  SET @grade = 'B';
END
ELSE
BEGIN
  SET @grade = 'C';
END

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: Adapted: T-SQL has no native FOR loop; WHILE is used instead.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
CREATE FUNCTION dbo.GetTotal (@a INT, @b INT)
RETURNS INT
AS
BEGIN
  RETURN @a + @b;
END

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
DECLARE @Arr TABLE (Id INT, Value VARCHAR(50));
INSERT INTO @Arr VALUES (1, 'One'), (2, 'Two');
arrays.notes: Adapted: T-SQL uses table variables instead of traditional arrays.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
DECLARE @Dict TABLE (KeyName VARCHAR(50) PRIMARY KEY, Value VARCHAR(100));
INSERT INTO @Dict VALUES ('key1', 'val1');
maps.notes: Adapted: Table variables act as dictionary/map structures.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
BEGIN TRY
  -- Code here
END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
  PRINT ERROR_MESSAGE();
END CATCH

comments.title: Comments
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment in T-SQL
/* Multi-line comment */
comments.notes: T-SQL uses -- for line comments and /* */ for blocks.

numbers.title: Numbers & Decimal Data
numbers.notes: T-SQL represents exact decimal precisions alongside standard integer types.

booleans.title: Booleans & Predicates
booleans.code:
-- Three-valued logic (TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN)
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND deleted_at IS NULL
booleans.notes: T-SQL evaluates predicates using declarative boolean conditions with NULL semantics.

type_casting.title: Type Casting (CAST/CONVERT)
type_casting.notes: T-SQL casts types using CAST(expr AS target_type) expressions.

strings.title: Strings & Text Literals
strings.code: SELECT 'String literal' AS col, N'Unicode text' AS unicode_col;
strings.notes: T-SQL encloses character literals in single quotes with optional N prefix for Unicode.

string_formatting.title: String Concatenation
string_formatting.code: SELECT CONCAT('User: ', username, ' (', email, ')') FROM users;
string_formatting.notes: T-SQL formats and joins textual columns using CONCAT or string concatenation operators.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching (LIKE & CASE)
pattern_matching.code:
SELECT CASE 
    WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'A'
    WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'B'
    ELSE 'C'
END AS grade
WHERE email LIKE '%@example.com';
pattern_matching.notes: T-SQL performs conditional classification via CASE WHEN and pattern search with LIKE.

range.title: Ranges (BETWEEN & LIMIT/OFFSET)
range.notes: T-SQL defines range intervals with BETWEEN and pagination ranges via LIMIT/OFFSET.

iterators.title: Cursors & Window Functions
iterators.notes: T-SQL processes ordered sequences set-by-set using window functions or procedural cursors.

oop_classes.title: Schemas & Tables (Entities)
oop_classes.notes: T-SQL structures entities through relational tables, constraints, and views.

lists.title: Tables & Arrays
lists.code:
-- Array or temporary result table
SELECT ARRAY[1, 2, 3] AS num_list;
lists.notes: T-SQL supports array column types or relation rowsets representing lists.

tuples.title: Rows & Composite Types
tuples.notes: T-SQL represents tuples as table rows or composite record types.

sets.title: Set Queries (UNION, INTERSECT)
sets.notes: T-SQL combines dataset results using relational algebra (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT).

modules_import.title: Schemas & Extensions
modules_import.code:
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp";
SET search_path TO my_schema, public;
modules_import.notes: T-SQL manages namespaces and modular capabilities through schemas and extensions.
